title: Dutch Hill Maple
about: Dutch Hill Maple began in 1968, when Dave Williams tapped 15 maple trees in his backyard and carried the sap through the woods in buckets to a boiling pan. More than half a century later it is still a family business in the hills of southern Onondaga County. Dave’s son Nate, who grew up sugaring with his father and brother, now leads it with his wife, Cristy.

The operation has grown to more than 7,500 taps, using tubing, vacuum and reverse osmosis, with a few buckets kept for tradition. In 2023 the family finished a new, climate-controlled sugarhouse on Woodmancy Road in Tully, the same year they made more than 5,000 gallons of syrup, a record for the farm. Alongside pure maple syrup, including a bourbon barrel-aged version, they make maple cream, maple candy and granulated maple sugar. They are part of the New York State Grown & Certified program for food safety and environmental practices.
The Williamses open the sugarhouse during New York’s Maple Weekends each March for tours and tastings. Year-round, you can find them at the CNY Regional Market on Saturdays.
facts: Maple syrup (incl. bourbon barrel-aged), maple cream, candy, sugar
